In the given table, the values of $x$ and $y$ satisfy the equation $2x - y = 2$:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline x & 0 & p \\ \hline y & q & 2 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

What would be the value of $p - q$?
stem:
In the given table, the values of $x$ and $y$ satisfy the equation $2x - y = 2$:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline x & 0 & p \\ \hline y & q & 2 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

What would be the value of $p - q$?
explanation: For $(0, q)$: $2(0) - q = 2 \implies -q = 2 \implies q = -2$. For $(p, 2)$: $2p - 2 = 2 \implies 2p = 4 \implies p = 2$. Thus $p - q = 2 - (-2) = 2 + 2 = 4$.
answer_origin: Independently solved and verified against source text
mappingReason: For $(0, q)$: $2(0) - q = 2 \implies -q = 2 \implies q = -2$. For $(p, 2)$: $2p - 2 = 2 \implies 2p = 4 \implies p = 2$. Thus $p - q = 2 - (-2) = 2 + 2 = 4$.
